issues.detail: The Greek 'καλαμω' (kalamō) is an instrumental case referring to a reed/cane. The Vietnamese 'đặt trên cây sậy' (placed on a reed) implies the sponge was resting on top of it, whereas the Greek implies the sponge was attached to or held by the reed (e.g., 'thấm đầy giấm vào cây sậy').

The Greek 'ει ερχεται' is a present active indicative, suggesting 'if [he] comes'. The Vietnamese 'có đến... chăng' adds a sense of speculative inquiry ('whether he will come') that slightly shifts the nuance from a conditional 'if' to a question of 'whether'.
